Issues: Sub goal h_log4_n_amc12a_2020_p10 has an issue:
The premises give a disjunction  
\( \text{Real.logb }4\,(n:\mathbb R)=0 \;\lor\; \text{Real.logb }4\,(n:\mathbb R)=4\).  
From this alone one cannot deduce that the value must be \(4\); it might be \(0\).

Indeed, \(\text{Real.logb }4\,x = \frac{\ln x}{\ln 4}\).  
Thus \(\text{Real.logb }4\,(n:\mathbb R)=0\) exactly when \(n=1\) (since \(\ln 1 = 0\)).  
The additional hypothesis \(h₀ : 0 < n\) does **not** exclude \(n=1\); \(1\) satisfies \(0<1\).

Consequently, for \(n=1\) we have \(h_{\text{cases}}\) true (the left side of the disjunction) while the desired conclusion \(\text{Real.logb }4\,(n:\mathbb R)=4\) is false. Hence the theorem is not provable from the given assumptions and is mathematically incorrect.

To make the statement correct one would need an extra condition ruling out the \(0\) case, e.g. \(n\neq 1\) or \(n>1\). With such a hypothesis the disjunction would force the second alternative, yielding the conclusion.
